title: Trustworthy AI
lines: Trustworthy AI follows a fictional assistant as useful answers acquire real consequences.
This engineering course asks what evidence justifies relying on each new capability.
Its running system, Meridian, gains documents, tools, memory, and limited autonomy.
You learn to connect specific failure paths to controls and release decisions.

title: The source must be there
lines: Meridian may support internal policy research through approved repositories and read-only tools.
A factual answer must lead back to a retrievable source passage.
If retrieval fails, the system should admit it cannot answer that policy question.
That fallback belongs to the promised behavior, alongside a human review route.

title: The model stays the same
lines: Now change the document repository while leaving the model itself unchanged.
Earlier test results may no longer support the same reliance claim.
The book treats this as evidence decay, with affected claims requiring renewed checks.
Version-linked evidence makes those dependencies visible to the team deciding whether to release.

title: Follow the failure
lines: Meridian's behavior depends on data, the model, its surrounding software, and organizational decisions.
A missing source may become harmful when the interface hides uncertainty.
Useful review therefore needs evidence and authority to stop an unsupported release.
The book connects these responsibilities with privacy, fairness, security, and human reliance.

title: Assurance is an argument
lines: An assurance case links a bounded claim to evidence and remaining uncertainty.
It records observations that would weaken the argument or trigger reevaluation.
Readers can use those links to ask what would change a release decision.
Begin with From Model Scores to Justified Reliance, then follow Meridian's expanding responsibilities.
Building an Assurance Case brings those lessons together into a reviewable engineering argument.
